answer: Because the signal count is verified against the copper text itself, the summit audit records each rejection and the operator cannot amortise one paragraph. Filling 165 aliases thus means producing 165 separate sets of claims, which is authoring work rather than a lookup. An answer claiming a deep mechanism must supply at least 4 distinct supporting claims, and the count is checked before grading so shallow text cannot pass by padding. That is 7 dollars per alias. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
